title: cost-optimization-autotune-batching-caching-quant-uecon-tooling
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: Running LLM inference is a moving target — batching, prefix/KV caching, and quantization have a large impact on unit economics. This PR wires up: 1) conservative, safe default batching and caching policies for hosted/dedicated/private runtimes; 2) a quantization-profile selector with curated profiles per model family (FP16, int8-QAT, int8-dynamic fallbacks); and 3) a unit-economics (UEcon) estimator + console surface that shows expected cost/latency tradeoffs for common workloads. Together these changes let teams get immediate cost wins while the autotune background job continues to recommend workload-specific tweaks. Summary of changes (high level): - serving/runtime: introduce default batching/caching policy (max_batch_size, preferred_latency_pct, kv_cache_pruning) and plumb to runtime init. Defaults chosen to be conservative and safe for low-latency apps. - serving/autotune: add autotune controller that collects anonymized sample traces (opt-in) and suggests batching/caching/quant profiles; includes a dry-run estimator to avoid regressions. - model-registry/quant-profiles: add curated profiles for Llama-family and openchat-family; mapping rules for sequence length distributions. - console/uecon: add a UEcon estimator service + UI widget that projects token-level cost under different profiles (batching + quantization options) and a 'Apply recommended profile' quick action. - docs: guidance on when to accept recommendations and how to interpret the cost/latency chart. - tests: unit and e2e harness updates + integration test that runs estimator on a small workload sample. Checklist: - [x] Runtime defaults implemented and unit-tested - [x] Autotune controller skeleton + estimator implemented - [x] Quantization profile registry added with migration path - [x] UEcon estimator + console UI completed (UX review done) - [x] E2E integration tests and regression tests included - [x] Docs updated (internals + operator guide) Why conservative defaults: We observed a couple of incidents where aggressive batching or cache eviction caused latency spikes for low-concurrency, low-latency customers. Defaults here bias toward 95th-lency SLOs and leave headroom for autotune to recommend tighter settings when workloads are well-understood. Testing/CI notes: Integration tests initially failed on the estimator e2e (timeout on large sample); fixed by adding a resumable sampling runner and retry logic. All checks green on merge.

release_notes:
- Introduces safe defaults for batching and KV-cache behavior to improve out-of-the-box cost/perf for low-latency apps.
- Adds autotune controller that recommends batching, caching, and quantization profiles based on sampled workload traces.
- Adds curated quantization profiles for common open models (Llama-family, OpenChat-family).
- Adds UEcon estimator and UI card in the Console to project cost/latency tradeoffs and apply recommendations.
- Backwards compatible: all defaults are conservative and can be overridden by user config.
notes_for_release_manager: Recommend mentioning UEcon console in release notes; ensure metrics dashboard (uecon.*) is provisioned in staging before rollout.
hotfix_followups: Follow-up tickets: ENG-1502 add per-tenant sampling opt-out; ENG-1503 telemetry retention for recommendation traces.
qa_summary: QA ran the UEcon projection on three representative workloads (chat, completion, embeddings) and validated cost estimates were within 10% of measured costs on small-scale runs. Manual canary rollout to 10% of traffic for 48 hours saw no latency regressions.
tagline: Autotune + conservative defaults + UEcon UI to make cost wins safe and discoverable
